title: Per-list-item `::marker` box sizing/alignment + wrapped list item indentation controls

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? When using `display: list-item` and `list-style-position: inside`, wrapped list item text is aligned with the start of the marker instead of the end of the marker. For example, suppose we have the following document: `index.html` ```html
  1. Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
  2. In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil.
  3. Stir both mixtures together.
  4. Fill muffin tray 3/4 full.
  5. Bake for 20 minutes.
  6. ???
  7. ???
  8. ???
  9. ???
  10. Yummy yummy profit.
``` If we pair it with the following stylesheet... `style.css` ```css ol { font-family: monospace; inline-size: 20ch; list-style-position: inside; list-style-type: decimal; & > li { display: block flow list-item; &::marker { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } } } ``` ...the document is rendered like this... ``` 1. Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. 2. In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil. 3. Stir both mixtures together. 4. Fill muffin tray 3/4 full. 5. Bake for 20 minutes. 6. ??? 7. ??? 8. ??? 9. ??? 10. Yummy yummy profit. ``` ...as opposed to this (the __desired block rendering__): ``` 1. Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. 2. In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil. 3. Stir both mixtures together. 4. Fill muffin tray 3/4 full. 5. Bake for 20 minutes. 6. ??? 7. ??? 8. ??? 9. ??? 10. Yummy yummy profit. ``` Note that the wrapped text indentation increases for item 10 compared to items 1-9. This is intentional. If we try to pad all markers to the length of the longest marker in the list, there will be too much padding for markers with few digits on lists that are hundreds/thousands/millions long. The layout algorithm would also be at the aggregate list items level (need to know marker sizes for all list items) instead of at the individual list item level. > The issue with the list item text alignment edge moving becomes less problematic as list size increases. You need an exponentially increasing number of list items to add additional decimal marker digits (enough to quickly exceed the viewport size). > > If we could set `min-inline-size: 3ch` and `text-align: end` on `::marker` elements, we can eliminate the list item text alignment edge change from 1 to 2 digits (e.g. `9.` to `10.`) as well. With decimal markers, this means a shift won't happen until 2 to 3 digits (e.g. `99.` to `100.`). > > ``` > 1. Mix flour, > baking powder, > sugar, and salt. > 2. In another bowl, > mix eggs, milk, > and oil. > 3. Stir both > mixtures > together. > 4. Fill muffin tray > 3/4 full. > 5. Bake for 20 > minutes. > 6. ??? > 7. ??? > 8. ??? > 9. ??? > 10. Yummy yummy > profit. > ... > 99. Before first > indent shift. > 100. After first > indent shift. > ``` > > This is what [Notion](https://www.notion.com) currently does with `
` soup and CSS flexbox, though it uses `text-align: center` instead so 1 digit markers are centered to 2 digit markers. If we use `list-style-position: outside` instead, markers are positioned before the inline start side of the parent `
    `'s CSS box. For example, the above document with `ol { list-style-position: outside; }` renders the all markers outside the `
      `'s CSS box: ``` Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil. Stir both mixtures together. Fill muffin tray 3/4 full. Bake for 20 minutes. ??? ??? ??? ??? Yummy yummy profit. ``` Most user agents hack around this by hardcoding the `
        ` (and `
          `) styles to include `padding-inline-start: 40px`. There isn't a way, however, to set the `
            ` element's `padding-inline-start` value to prevent overflow for arbitrarily long marker texts (e.g. ordered lists that are hundreds/thousands/millions long). Even if there were, `list-style-position: outside` also forces the markers to be right-aligned. This is unlike in the desired block rendering which has the markers left-aligned with no additional spacing between the marker and list item text. ### What solutions exist today? We can wrap list item contents in a `
            ` and use CSS flexbox to treat the `::marker` pseudo-element and `
            ` as separate flex items. `::marker`, however, currently doesn't support CSS box sizing (e.g. `min-inline-size`) or alignment (e.g. `text-align`) properties. Instead, we'd need to drop `display: list-item` in favor of CSS counters and `::before` (less restricted than `::marker`). For example: `index.html` ```html
            1. Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
            2. In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil.
            3. Stir both mixtures together.
            4. Fill muffin tray 3/4 full.
            5. Bake for 20 minutes.
            6. ???
            7. ???
            8. ???
            9. ???
            10. Yummy yummy profit.
            ``` `style.css` ```css ol { /* debug */ border: dashed blue 1px; padding: 0; counter-reset: list-item; font-family: monospace; inline-size: 20ch; & > li { counter-increment: list-item; display: block flex; &::before { /* debug */ color: blue; content: counter(list-item) "."; flex: none; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-inline-end: 1ch; min-inline-size: 3ch; text-align: end; } & > div { display: inline flow; } } } ``` Sample render (using `
          1. ` to show longer markers): It's not clear if this introduces accessibility issues (something similar to how [Safari stops announcing lists in the accessibility tree if `list-style: none` is used](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/list-style#accessibility)). ### How would you solve it? #### Per-List-Item `::marker` Box Sizing/Alignment Support setting box sizing (e.g. `flex`, `margin-inline-end`, `min-inline-size`) and alignment (e.g. `text-align`) properties on `::marker` elements. This would also need support for setting the `` value on ` list-item` to `flex` (e.g. `li { display: block flex list-item; }`). Only `flow` and `flow-root` are currently supported. We get the nice property of `li { display: inline flow list-item; }` automatically ignoring certain box sizing attributes (e.g. `min-inline-size`) on `::marker` elements so inline lists are rendered without extra spacing like this: ``` 1. Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt. 2. In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil. 3. Stir both mixtures together. 4. Fill muffin tray 3/4 full. 5. Bake for 20 minutes. 6. ??? 7. ??? 8. ??? 9. ??? 10. Yummy yummy profit. ``` #### Per-List-Item Wrapped List Item Indentation The `
            ` element has a `::details-content` pseudo-element CSS selector which lets users select all subsequent elements after its first child (a ``). Essentially, the DOM tree looks like this: ```html
            <::marker/> Show/Hide <::details-content>

            ...

            ...

            ``` It might be possible to add a `::list-item-content` pseudo-element CSS selector which does something similar. The DOM tree would look like this: ```html
            1. <::marker/> <::list-item-content> Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
            2. <::marker/> <::list-item-content> In another bowl, mix eggs, milk, and oil.
            3. <::marker/> <::list-item-content> Yummy yummy profit.
            ``` This `::list-item-content` pseudo-element effectively exists today with a default `display: contents` style. We need it to have a `display: inline flow` value instead. > `
            ` + `` is a kind of strange `
              ` + `
            • ` pair since `` by default uses `display: list-item` + `list-style-position: inside` in many user agents. > > It also has a similar indentation problem with its marker (`list-style-type: disclosure-closed` + `list-style-type: disclosure-open`). > > This would also solve the issue since we can use `details > summary::list-item-content { display: inline flow; }` so wrapped text doesn't wrap below the disclosure triangle. > > With `::list-item-content`, its DOM tree would look like this: > > ```html >
              > > <::marker/> > <::list-item-content> > Show/Hide > > > <::details-content> >

              ...

              >

              ...

              > >
              > ``` ### Anything else? _No response_
